notes_summary: Mid-market product analytics org. Completed hosted API POC; now negotiating Dedicated commit, burst and overage terms. Security + procurement are gating signoff.
notes:
Background:
- Cerulean Horizon builds an in-product analytics and guidance layer used by product managers and customers for adoption insights.
- Started with Redwood hosted API in Dec 2025 (trial + small pilot for 3 features). POC metrics show 45% token cost reduction vs naive calls after prefix caching.

Engagement timeline (shorthand):
- 2025-12-02: Intro demo (AE Maya, SE Dev) — showed hosted API flow and retry/fallback.
- 2026-01-12: Fireflies call — POC results review (ff_2026-02-18_ch-cerulean-poc).
- 2026-02-18: Dedicated demo + latency benchmarks (can sustain 120 QPS 99th < 180ms on test model).
- 2026-02-25: Initial pricing proposal delivered (tiered commits + optional burst).
- 2026-03-03: Legal/security kick-off — requested SOC2 docs and KMS integration notes.
- 2026-03-10: Negotiation call re: commit ramp and overage math.

POC / technical notes:
- Workloads: chat assistant (multi-turn), embeddings for semantic search, and reranking for recommendations.
- Latency target: 95th <= 250ms for UI chat; throughput target: steady 60–120 QPS during peak.
- Host API pilot satisfied functional requirements; edge-case hallucination rate acceptable after prompt tuning.
- Key requirement: predictable monthly unit economics — product team prefers reserved capacity model to cap variable cost.

Pricing / packaging negotiation (current status):
- Redwood initial Dedicated proposal: 3 commit tiers (small/med/large) expressed as reserved vGPU-hours + baseline throughput. Proposal attached in Drive.
- Cerulean counterpoints: prefer commit expressed as committed throughput (tokens/sec or QPS equivalent) and a 3-month ramp (50% month1, 75% month2, 100% month3).
- Burst: ask for short-term burst (up to 2x committed throughput) for 2x daily peaks, charged at explicit burst rate (proposed 1.6x of committed unit rate).
- Overage: they request capped overage pricing (not open-ended). Redwood proposed overage at 1.8x per-unit; Cerulean pushing for 1.4x with a monthly cap.
- Commitment term: 12-month SOW preferred by Redwood for pricing; Cerulean considering 9–12 months with early-termination safety (pro-rated with penalty).
- Ramp schedule: product team wants clear ability to increase commit mid-term with 30-day notice and pro-rated pricing. SE noted technical frictionless scale but billing needs clarity.

Security / compliance notes:
- Need SOC2 attestation and architecture diagram for VPC peering.
- KMS integration required for encryption of logs and KV cache.
- Data residency — want US-only logs retention for 13 months.
- Legal asked for audit_logging details and retention SLAs.

Quotes / direct snippets:
- CTO: "We like the hosted performance data, but our CFO insists on a fixed predictable committed spend for FY27."
- Product lead: "If you can give a safe burst window and a reasonable cap on overage, we can sign the SOW this quarter."

Open questions for Redwood sales/ops:
- Can we map the proposed vGPU-hour commits to their desired QPS/tokens/sec baseline? (SE to produce mapping table).
- Is there flexibility on overage multiplier or a monthly overage cap? Finance to advise.
- Can the ramp schedule be implemented in billing (50/75/100) without admin overhead? Ops to confirm.

Next steps (near term):
- SE Dev to deliver commit->throughput mapping and expected tail latencies by 2026-03-14.
- AE Maya to push updated pricing sheet (with alternative overage cap) by 2026-03-17.
- Legal/security to exchange SOC2 + KMS docs; CISO sync scheduled for 2026-03-20.
- Procurement to review SOW once pricing adjustments accepted.

Internal notes (AE/SE):
- High win probability if we can align on overage cap and ramp billing.
- Watch churn risk: product team very cost sensitive; if overage is too punitive they may fallback to hybrid model (hosted + on-demand on cloud).
- Prepare a 9-month variant SOW with slightly higher unit price to accommodate their preference.
